scenes.text: Blind as a bat? Bats aren't blind at all.
Every one of the more than one thousand bat species has working eyes.
Big fruit bats, called flying foxes, have huge eyes and mostly find their way by sight.
Many of them can't even echolocate.
Smaller bats use echolocation to catch tiny insects, but they still use their eyes for landmarks far away.
Studies even suggest some bats can see ultraviolet light.
What other animal myth did you believe?

title: Bats aren't blind 🦇
caption: "Blind as a bat" is a myth: all bats can see. Flying foxes rely mostly on their big eyes, and echolocating bats still use vision for long-range landmarks. 🦇
